title: Preparing Students for the Future: A Need to Integrate Entomology and Technology Education
content: Modern technology has become an integral part of entomological work, with advances increasingly relying on tools such as artificial intelligence (AI), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), DNA barcoding, geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, big data, and gene editing. More than ever, students are expected to be proficient in these technologies while also maintaining traditional knowledge of insects. My own undergraduate journey began in computer science, where I developed a strong foundation in computer and programming skills. After switching majors to natural resource conservation, I had the opportunity to work in Dr. Silvana V. Paula-Moraes’ entomology lab at the University of Florida (UF) for two years. During that time, I noticed a surprising disconnect: students are not often taught how to bridge biology and technology. If students are expected to be both tech savvy and bug smart, we need support and opportunities to develop skills in both areas to excel.
